page_hint: Ch 20 §4 Table 20-1 note and Ch 20 §8 aggregate-req/s note
observed: The same chapter later says sustaining 80 req/s needs ~41–46 hosts, with the governing case-(ii) prefill screen giving 44 raw and 46 with the ρ derate.
root_cause: Stale summary after the full screen set was added.
correction: Change the table note to 'sustaining 80 req/s needs ~41–46 hosts (41 KV, 43 KV with ρ, 44 case-(ii) prefill raw, 46 case-(ii) prefill with ρ)' or explicitly scope 41–43 to the KV screen only.
acceptance_test: All 80 req/s host-count statements in Ch 20 agree on the same screen set and range.

quoted_clause: The break-even against a statically provisioned, peak-sized 23-host fleet ($460/hr = 23 × $20, no control plane) sits at 21 hosts, i.e. sustained demand ≤ ~41.5 rps: above that, autoscaling costs more than the peak-sized fleet it replaces.
observed: The break-even uses the 21-host KV screen capacity (21×17/8.6≈41.5 rps), but the chapter's own governing 23-host sizing at 40 rps includes the case-(ii) prefill screen with the ρ derate. At 41.5 rps the case-(ii) prefill screen would require more than 21 hosts, so the autoscaled cost would not be 21×$20+$40.
evidence: 41.5 rps × 9,200 = 381,800 prefill tok/s; ÷16,870 = 22.6 raw hosts; ÷0.95 = 23.8 → 24 hosts. 24×$20+$40=$520/hr > $460/hr. Also a static 23-host fleet has analytic KV capacity 23×1.977≈45.5 rps, so the comparison is only valid up to that capacity.
root_cause: Break-even arithmetic was computed on the KV screen alone without applying the chapter's full governing screens.
correction: Either label the break-even as 'KV-screen-only' and recompute the full-screen break-even, or state that the static 23-host comparison is valid only up to its ~45.5 rps analytic capacity and that the full governing screen changes the autoscaled host count near 41.5 rps.
acceptance_test: The break-even demand is consistent with the host-count function used for the autoscaled fleet (KV-only or full governing) and with the static fleet's serviceable capacity.

quoted_clause: The achieved MFU is below the 35% ideal.
observed: 35% is introduced as a conservative planning MFU, not an ideal hardware limit. Calling it 'ideal' can imply that 35% is a physical ceiling or that actual performance is below an idealized 35%.
evidence: Earlier in the same section: 'Ch 20 uses the conservative 35% planning MFU (Ch 8)'; the hardware peak is 100% dense, and 35% is a planning assumption.
root_cause: Imprecise label for the 35% efficiency assumption.
correction: Change to 'The achieved MFU is below the 35% planning MFU' or 'the 35% figure is already a planning assumption, not an ideal'.
acceptance_test: No sentence describes the 35% planning MFU as an ideal or hardware peak.

quoted_clause: The 21-host KV-screen sizing has an analytical capacity of ≈ 41.5 req/s ≈ 1.04× peak (C_analytic = 21 × 17/8.6); the 22-host ρ-derated sizing gives ≈ 41.3 req/s ≈ 1.03×, and served demand still caps at the 40 rps peak. The KV-screen sizing passes its own screens at ≈ 1× peak; the 2× row is what a soak pool must sustain.
observed: The sentence compares a 21-host analytic capacity with a 22-host ρ-derated capacity, and then says the KV-screen sizing 'passes its own screens'. A reader can infer that 21 hosts passes all relevant screens, but Ch 20's full governing screen is 23 hosts (case-(ii) prefill with ρ), and 21 hosts under the same ρ derate has only ≈39.4 req/s effective capacity.
root_cause: Mixed bases (analytic vs ρ-derated) and ambiguous 'own screens'.
correction: Clarify: 'The 21-host analytic KV screen has 41.5 req/s, but under the same ρ derate it provides 39.4 req/s; the 22-host ρ-derated KV screen provides 41.3 req/s. The full governing screen is 23 hosts (case-(ii) prefill with ρ).' Remove or qualify 'passes its own screens' to mean only the KV screen.
acceptance_test: The passage distinguishes analytic, ρ-derated, and full governing capacities without implying 21 hosts satisfies all screens.

quoted_clause: a one-sided binomial test (alpha = 0.05) returns p ≈ 6.4e-5
observed: For 12 observed legal-subset failures among ≈360 legal-subset canary requests, with an incumbent baseline of ≈0.83% (expected ≈3), the one-sided binomial p-value is not ≈6.4e-5; it is approximately 0.005 (0.5%).
evidence: n=360, p0=0.0083, observed x=12. Poisson approximation λ=2.988 gives P(X≥12)≈0.0052; exact binomial is of the same order. 6.4e-5 would correspond to a much smaller expected count or a larger observed count.
correction: Replace with the correct one-sided binomial p-value (e.g., p≈0.005) or state the exact computation method and result. The gate still fires at alpha=0.05, so the conclusion can remain.
acceptance_test: A binomial CDF calculation for n=360, p0=0.0083, x≥12 matches the printed p-value within rounding.

quoted_clause: a homogeneous cluster sized at ~17–19 hosts clears both budgets on the 40%-MFU prefill / 24.1 GB input-only-KV sensitivity
observed: Using the stated 24.1 GB per request and 436 GB KV budget per host, 19 hosts do not hold the 344 in-flight requests at peak; 20 hosts are required. Thus the 17–19 range does not clear the KV budget.
evidence: 344 in-flight × 24.1 GB = 8,290.4 GB. 19 hosts × 436 GB = 8,284 GB, short by 6.4 GB. Equivalently 344 ÷ (436/24.1) = 19.02 → 20. If using whole-slot floor 18, 344/18=19.11 → 20.
root_cause: Rounding of 24.1 GB or approximate range allowed 19 to be treated as sufficient.
correction: Change to '~17–20 hosts' or use a consistent rounded KV size (e.g., 24.0 GB) and state the approximation. If the intent is a sensitivity, say 'approximately 17–20' rather than 'clears'.
acceptance_test: The stated host range satisfies both the 40%-MFU prefill screen and the 24.1 GB KV screen at 40 rps.

quoted_clause: a ~21–32-host fleet at the canonical peak (Ch 17/20/24)
observed: The canonical peak host-count set in Ch 20 and Ch 25 includes 23 hosts (ρ-derated case-(ii) prefill screen) and 34 hosts (full 70%×95%+N−1 policy under case (ii)), in addition to 21/22/32. The 21–32 range omits the governing 23 and the full-policy 34 case-(ii) values.
evidence: Ch 20: 21 KV, 22 ρ-KV, 22 raw case-(ii) prefill, 23 ρ case-(ii), 32 KV policy, 34 case-(ii) policy. Ch 25 ADR 0015 R1: 21/32 case (i), 22/34 case (ii).
root_cause: Summary range copied from a subset of screens (case (i)/KV policy) without including case-(ii) full policy.
correction: Change to '~21–34 hosts' or specify '~21–32 under case (i)/KV policy and ~22–34 under case (ii)'.
acceptance_test: The Ch 23 host range matches the full screen set reported in Ch 20/25 for the canonical peak.

quoted_clause: a scaled-down illustration, ~4× below the canonical peak screens (21 hosts KV / 19–22 prefill / 32 policy) that the Red Team's checks below apply.
observed: This summary of canonical peak screens omits the ρ-derated case-(ii) prefill screen (23 hosts) and the full-policy case-(ii) value (34 hosts) used in Ch 20 and Ch 25. If Ch 24 intentionally uses raw screens only, it should say so.
root_cause: Abbreviated screen list not aligned with the book's full planning screens.
correction: Either expand to '21 KV / 19–22 raw prefill / 23 ρ-derated case-(ii) / 32–34 policy' or add 'raw screens only; ρ and full-policy values are in Ch 20/25'.
acceptance_test: A reader can reconcile Ch 24's peak-screen summary with Ch 20/25 without assuming missing values.

quoted_clause: the canonical fleet is 21 hosts at peak.
observed: 21 hosts is the KV-screen headline, not the full governing fleet size. Ch 20's governing pre-policy screen is 23 hosts, and the full policy is 32/34 depending on case.
evidence: Ch 20: 21 = ⌈344/17⌉; 23 = ⌈21.81/0.95⌉; 32/34 under 70%×95%+N−1. Ch 25 ADR 0015: 21-host KV-screen headline / 32-host N−1 policy (case i), 22/34 case ii.
root_cause: Using the KV-screen number as 'the canonical fleet' without qualification.
correction: Change to 'the canonical KV-screen fleet is 21 hosts at peak (23 under Ch 20's ρ-derated case-(ii) prefill screen; 32/34 under the full policy)' or 'the 21-host KV-screen baseline'.
acceptance_test: ADR 0016's host count is clearly scoped to the KV screen and does not contradict Ch 20/25.

quoted_clause: 0.0052 is an expected count — poisoned chunks per top-5 retrieval (≈0.52% of one chunk) — whereas the §4.1 target is a probability: the fraction of retrievals returning at least one poisoned chunk, 1 − (1 − p)^5 ≈ 0.005197 (≈0.52%).
observed: The phrase '≈0.52% of one chunk' is an awkward unit for an expected count and can blur the distinction between count and probability.
evidence: The expected count is 0.0052 chunks per retrieval; the probability is 0.005197 retrievals with ≥1 poisoned chunk. Both are numerically close but dimensionally different.
root_cause: Attempt to make the count intuitively comparable to the probability introduced a nonstandard unit.
correction: Rewrite as '0.0052 poisoned chunks per retrieval (i.e., 0.52% in count units)' and keep the probability sentence separate.
acceptance_test: The count and probability are stated with distinct units and no 'percent of one chunk' phrasing.

quoted_clause: A page of prose is roughly 500–700 tokens, so two to three pages plus retrieved sections lands in the low thousands; the exact 9,200/300 split is the canonical scenario imported from Ch 4, Table 4-2 rather than elicited here, and the pilot's tokenizer run replaces it.
observed: The customer's page estimate ('two to three pages') suggests a few thousand tokens, but the bound then uses 9,200 input tokens. Although the text says the exact split is imported, the juxtaposition can make the 9,200 look elicited from the page estimate.
evidence: 2–3 pages × 500–700 tokens = 1,000–2,100 tokens before retrieved context; 9,200 includes an 8,000-token retrieved context assumption from the canonical scenario.
root_cause: Worked-example dialogue blends customer language with canonical imported values without a sharper break.
correction: Add a sentence: 'The 8,000-token retrieved-context component is not implied by the page estimate; it is the canonical scenario assumption that the pilot tokenizer run will replace.'
acceptance_test: A reader cannot infer that 9,200 tokens was derived from the customer's two-to-three-page statement.

quoted_clause: business-hours basis: 10 rps average × 8 h × 260 workdays, Ch 16 arithmetic — so the monthly denominator averages ~2.4 rps
observed: The formula as printed omits the conversion from hours to seconds and the division by 12 months, so it does not by itself yield 6.24M requests/month or 2.4 rps.
evidence: 10 rps × 8 h × 3,600 s/h × 260 workdays ÷ 12 = 6,240,000 requests/month; 6,240,000 ÷ (30×24×3,600) ≈ 2.4 rps calendar-month average.
root_cause: Abbreviated formula relies on Ch 16 for missing factors.
correction: Write the full expression or add '× 3,600 s/h ÷ 12'.
acceptance_test: The printed formula reproduces 6.24M requests/month without external lookup.

quoted_clause: a decode-only ceiling of 100% MFU (≤141 rps — 7B FP16, ~500 output tokens/request, H100); with the ~500-token prefill included the total request rate is ~71 rps at 100% MFU (~21–28 rps at 30–40% MFU)
observed: Decode is the bandwidth-bound leg in the book's model; MFU is a compute-efficiency metric. Calling the decode ceiling '100% MFU' can imply the 141 rps limit is compute-bound or that MFU is the right denominator for decode.
evidence: Ch 2/6/22 establish low-batch decode as bandwidth-bound; a 7B FP16 decode ceiling should be framed as an assumed aggregate token-rate or HBM-bandwidth-limited rate, not MFU, unless the 141 rps is explicitly derived from a compute budget.
root_cause: Borrowing the prefill MFU language for an illustrative decode rate.
correction: Reword to 'an assumed 100%-efficiency aggregate token-rate ceiling' or '100% of the illustrative 7B H100 token budget', and if MFU is retained, state it is a proxy for overall efficiency, not a compute-MFU claim.
acceptance_test: The passage does not use MFU as the primary metric for a bandwidth-bound decode ceiling without qualification.
